fields.label: Averaging (population = weighted by where residents live)

legend_note: The pollutant that does the most health damage, averaged over four years and weighted by where each commune's residents live. The WHO guideline is 5 µg/m³ and the EU limit from 2030 is 10. Only about 4% of communes are under 5; the median is 7.3; Grenoble, the Lille conurbation and Paris sit at 11–12. Values fell about a fifth between 2022 and 2024, partly cleaner air and partly a wet 2024, so the four-year mean is a fair central estimate and the most recent years run lower.

legend_note: Mostly traffic exhaust. WHO guideline 10 µg/m³, EU limit from 2030 20. 92% of communes are under 10, but inner Paris averages 31 and Marseille, Lyon and Nice about 21. This is a 1 km background estimate: it cannot see the street, so anyone living on a main road breathes noticeably more than the value here. Treat it as the floor.

fields.label: SOMO35 in the worst of the four years

legend_note: Ozone is a summer, sunshine pollutant, and it runs opposite to the other two: highest in the hills and the south-east, lower in city centres, where traffic fumes break it down. SOMO35 adds up every day's excess over 70 µg/m³ (daily maximum 8-hour mean) across the year, so it measures total yearly exposure, not the worst day. It swings with the weather far more than PM2.5 or NO₂: a hot summer like 2022 raises it by half. That is why four years are averaged.
